scams.location: Strasbourg Cathedral, Cathedral Square, Place Kléber, Petite France, Train Station
scams.story: Teams of scammers approach tourists with clipboards asking if they speak English, then request signatures for a fake 'deaf charity' petition. While you're distracted reading or signing, accomplices pickpocket your bags or pockets. After signing, they demand a donation, pointing to text claiming you agreed to donate. The petition is always in English (a red flag in France) and they use exaggerated sign language to appear hearing-impaired.
red_flags: Petition written in English rather than French
Request for immediate cash donation after signing
how_to_avoid: Never stop for clipboard petitioners
Say 'Non' firmly and keep walking
Never sign anything on the street
Keep hands on your belongings when approached

scams.location: Cathedral steps, Petite France, Tourist walkways, Christmas markets
scams.story: A vendor grabs your hand and begins wrapping colorful string around your wrist before you can refuse. Within seconds, they've tied a difficult-to-remove bracelet and demand €10-20 for the 'gift.' They become aggressive if you refuse to pay, and may follow you while creating a scene. Sometimes an accomplice uses the distraction to pickpocket you.
red_flags: Anyone reaching for your hand unexpectedly
People with string or craft materials visible
Overly friendly strangers near tourist spots
how_to_avoid: Keep hands in pockets when walking through tourist areas
Say 'Non' firmly and keep walking
Pull your hand away immediately if they try to grab it
Carry small scissors to cut yourself free if necessary

scams.location: Near bridges, Pedestrian areas, Tourist walkways, Pont du Corbeau
scams.story: A stranger bends down near you and 'finds' a gold ring, then asks if you dropped it. When you say no, they examine it and claim it's marked '18K gold' and must be valuable. They offer to sell it for a fraction of its 'worth' or ask for a finder's fee. The ring is worthless brass. While engaging you, an accomplice may be pickpocketing you.
red_flags: Someone conveniently finding jewelry right next to you
Ring appears suspiciously shiny and new
Persistent pressure to buy or give money
how_to_avoid: Simply say 'non' and walk away
Don't engage in conversation
Be aware of accomplices nearby
Keep hands on belongings

scams.location: Tram Lines B and C, Gare Centrale, Crowded tram stops, Cathedral area tram stops
scams.story: Pickpockets work the crowded Strasbourg trams, especially Lines B and C that serve tourist areas. They operate during rush hours and at boarding/exiting when movement is chaotic. Teams use distraction techniques—one person blocks your path or bumps into you while an accomplice steals from your bag or pocket. They often exit quickly just as doors close.
red_flags: Groups crowding around you on the tram
how_to_avoid: Keep bags in front with hands on them
Don't keep valuables in back pockets
Be extra vigilant when boarding and exiting
If bumped, immediately check belongings

scams.location: Near Strasbourg Cathedral, Boat tour departure points, Outside tourist attractions
scams.story: Unlicensed sellers approach tourists outside popular attractions offering 'discounted' tickets for boat tours, cathedral tower climbs, or other experiences. The tickets are fake, already used, or for non-existent tours. The seller disappears before you discover the scam. Some pose as official guides offering 'special access.'
red_flags: Sellers approaching you rather than at official counters
how_to_avoid: Buy tickets only from official ticket offices
Book tours through established companies
Be suspicious of 'special deals' from strangers
Research official prices beforehand

scams.location: Christkindelsmärik (main market), Place Broglie, Place Kléber, All Christmas market locations
scams.story: Strasbourg's famous Christmas markets attract over 2 million visitors annually, creating ideal conditions for pickpockets. The dense crowds, distracting lights, and hands occupied with food and drinks make tourists easy targets. Professional teams work the markets, using distraction techniques or simply taking advantage of the chaos. Valuable items disappear from bags, pockets, and even hands.
red_flags: Anyone pressing against you in crowds
how_to_avoid: Wear cross-body bags in front
Keep zippers secured and hands on bags
Leave valuables at hotel
Be extra vigilant in crowded market lanes
Visit during less crowded morning hours

scams.location: Strasbourg Airport, Gare Centrale, Hotel pickups at night
scams.story: Some taxi drivers target tourists unfamiliar with local fares. They may claim the meter is broken and quote inflated prices, take unnecessarily long routes, or select the higher night/weekend tariff during regular hours. From the airport to city center, legitimate fare is approximately €40-50 during the day.
red_flags: Meter showing night rate during daytime
how_to_avoid: Insist on using the meter
Know the approximate fare in advance
Use GPS to follow the route
Consider using Uber or official taxi apps
Get receipt for any disputes

scams.location: Tourist areas, Near borders, Tram stops, Quiet streets at night
scams.story: Criminals pose as plainclothes police, quickly flashing fake badges. They claim they need to check your wallet for counterfeit currency or verify your identity due to 'border security.' While examining your wallet or documents, they steal cash. Being near the German border, they may claim special authority for 'cross-border checks.' Real French police don't randomly check tourists' wallets on the street.
red_flags: Plainclothes person claiming to be police
Quick flash of badge without allowing inspection
Request to see your wallet or cash
how_to_avoid: Ask to see official ID clearly and note badge number
Insist on going to nearest police station before showing documents
Never hand over your wallet to anyone on the street
Call 17 (police) if suspicious

scams.location: Cathedral Square restaurants, Petite France terraces, Tourist-heavy areas
scams.story: Tourist restaurants near major attractions use tactics to overcharge visitors. Different menus in different languages show different prices. Waiters bring expensive bottled water without asking, add items not ordered, or charge premium prices for Alsatian specialties. Some insist on automatic gratuity despite service being included in French prices.
how_to_avoid: Ask for the French menu and compare prices
Request 'une carafe d'eau' (tap water) - it's free
Check bill carefully against what you ordered
Know that service is included in French prices
Walk a few streets from major monuments for better value

scams.location: Standalone ATMs, ATMs in tourist areas, Private ATMs (Euronet, Travelex)
scams.story: Criminals attach skimming devices to ATMs that capture card data and PINs. Private ATMs like Euronet charge excessive fees and poor exchange rates. Some offer Dynamic Currency Conversion at terrible rates while making it seem like a benefit. Card trap devices may also be used - your card gets stuck and a 'helpful' stranger watches you enter your PIN.
red_flags: Card slot feels loose or bulky
Prompts to convert to your home currency
Stranger offering help when card gets stuck
how_to_avoid: Use ATMs inside bank branches only
Cover keypad when entering PIN
Wiggle card slot before inserting
Decline dynamic currency conversion
If card gets stuck, don't leave - call bank immediately

scams.location: Crowded tourist areas, Cathedral entrances, Tram stops, Markets
scams.story: A well-dressed person 'accidentally' bumps into you, spills something on you, or drops items near your feet. While apologizing profusely and helping clean you up or as you helpfully bend down to assist, an accomplice steals from your bag or pockets. Another variation: someone points out a 'stain' on your back to distract you.
red_flags: Someone spilling on you in a tourist area
Overly apologetic stranger insisting on helping
Someone pointing out stains on your clothing
how_to_avoid: If spilled on, immediately check belongings and move away
Don't let strangers touch your clothing
Be suspicious of any unusual contact
Keep bags secured in front of you

scams.location: Near Cathedral, Tourist photo spots, Petite France bridges
scams.story: Unlicensed vendors sell cheap souvenirs, 'artwork,' or photos at massively inflated prices. They target tourists at photo spots, offering to take pictures then demanding payment for the 'service.' Some sell 'authentic Alsatian' items that are actually mass-produced imports. They become aggressive when you refuse to buy or try to negotiate.
red_flags: Vendors without official permits or stalls
Claims of 'authentic local craft' at very low prices
how_to_avoid: Buy souvenirs from established shops
Decline offers from street vendors
Never hand your camera/phone to unsolicited helpers
Know that most legitimate vendors have fixed prices displayed
